claims.claim: Perkins says he does not frontload information but lets it trickle out.
claims.source: Christopher Perkins, The Dungeon Master Experience: T'wit, Dungeon 197, 2011

claims.claim: Perkins says that whenever the characters arrive in a new village, town or city he gives them local rumours, some true and some false.
claims.source: Christopher Perkins, The Dungeon Master Experience: Lies My DM Told Me, Dungeon 197, 2011
claims.quote: new village, town, or city, I pepper them with local
claims.page: column: Lies My DM Told Me

claims.claim: Perkins advises that when in doubt the DM should tell the players things that are true, noting that old D&D adventures carried more true rumours than false ones.
claims.source: Christopher Perkins, The Dungeon Master Experience: Lies My DM Told Me, Dungeon 197, 2011
claims.quote: When in doubt, tell the players things that are true.
claims.page: column: Lies My DM Told Me, Lessons Learned

claims.claim: Perkins says the trick with human names is finding names that sound human yet seem grounded in a world of fantasy rather than reality.

claims.claim: Winninger tells the DM to give the home settlement a rumour mill, a place where adventurers gather to swap boasts, rumours and legends.

claims.claim: Winninger sets the minimum population of a home base at two interesting NPCs, arguing it is better to develop two really good ideas than four or five mediocre ones.

claims.claim: The DUNGEON staff's writers' guidelines state that read-aloud text makes no reference to the viewer.
claims.source: The DUNGEON Staff, DUNGEON Submission Guidelines, Read-Aloud Text section
claims.quote: does not make any reference to the viewer

claims.claim: The DUNGEON guidelines tell writers to avoid phrases such as "you see" and "as you enter the room" in read-aloud text because they assume player action.
claims.source: The DUNGEON Staff, DUNGEON Submission Guidelines, Read-Aloud Text section
claims.quote: Avoid phrases such as “you see,” “as you enter the

claims.claim: The DUNGEON guidelines cap read-aloud text: it should only rarely run more than a few sentences.
claims.source: The DUNGEON Staff, DUNGEON Submission Guidelines, Read-Aloud Text section
claims.quote: should only rarely run more than a few sentences

claims.claim: The DUNGEON guidelines say long sections of read-aloud text are better served as player handouts.
claims.source: The DUNGEON Staff, DUNGEON Submission Guidelines, Read-Aloud Text section
claims.quote: are better served as player handouts

claims.claim: The DUNGEON guidelines tell writers to keep descriptions of creatures out of read-aloud text, because a creature's position and activity depend on circumstances.
claims.source: The DUNGEON Staff, DUNGEON Submission Guidelines, Read-Aloud Text section
claims.quote: descriptions of any creatures in the room

claims.claim: The DUNGEON editors say they greatly dislike printing the words "This room is empty" in the magazine.
claims.source: The DUNGEON Staff, DUNGEON Submission Guidelines, The Adventure's Encounters
claims.quote: printing the words “This room is empty”
